simple.meaning: עַתִּיק (ʻattîyq) is a Hebrew word meaning “removed , i.e. weaned ; also antique.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: עַתִּיק (H6267) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at 1 Chronicles 4:22, with occurrences in 1 Chronicles, Isaiah.

definitions.full: H6267. attiq [ עַתִּיק ] adjective removed, old ; — 1 removed , מִשָּׁדָ֑יִם עַתִּיקֵי Isa 28:9 i.e. weaned (|| מֵחָלָד גְּמוּלֵי ; on construct see Ges § 130a ). 2 old, ancient (Aramaism: עַתִּיק , , old ), עַתִּיקִים הַדְּדָרִים 1Chr 4:22 . עַתִּיק adjective advanced, aged (Biblical Hebrew (as Aramaism), √ עתק , q. v.); — construct ( מַיָּא -) ׳ע יוֺמִין one advanced, aged, in days Dan 7:9 , 13 , 22 (compare Syriac Ecclus 25:4 and elsewhere, PS 3011 ).

occurrences.englishText: and Jokim, and the men of Cozeba, and Joash, and Saraph, who had dominion in Moab, and Jashubilehem. These records are ancient.
